# Help people understand and revise a plan

Make a planning application's timing, trade-offs, and revisions understandable.
A readable Gantt view is a means to that purpose, not a commitment to a particular
market, storage service, scheduler, or date model. Keep desired outcomes distinct
from revisable implementation conclusions and let feedback change the direction.

This is a fictional worked example commissioned by the SpecSpec project owner.
STORY.md labels every simulated user/AI turn; none is an actual external client's
instruction or technical sign-off. Git records real specification and code stages.

# Make timing readable

Show task names and date ranges alongside aligned timeline bars. Supply a textual equivalent, keyboard-accessible controls, and horizontal scrolling rather than silently hiding long plans.

Origin: STORY.md, simulated opening request.

# Keep project text and invalid input safe

Treat names and imported data as text, not executable markup. Reject invalid input before replacing a valid plan and explain problems without discarding current work.

Origin: STORY.md, simulated opening clarification.

# Learn without erasing the earlier rationale

Use separate intention and conclusion nodes. When the simulated user redirects, physically delete the obsolete dependent branch, keep its explanations in prior Git commits, and record the next experiment honestly. No approval statuses or depth-based confidence scores.

Origin: STORY.md, simulated AI review-boundary clarification.

# Plan a business portfolio

Help a manager see multiple projects together, with each task assigned to a project. Origin: STORY.md, simulated opening user.

# Forecast business-day dependencies

Forecast tasks from durations and finish-to-start dependencies using Monday-Friday working days. Origin: STORY.md, simulated opening user.

# Plan named team members

Track the team member responsible for each task. Origin: STORY.md, simulated opening user.

# Avoid double-booking automatically

Eventually delay work automatically when the same member is booked twice. Origin: STORY.md, simulated opening user; not delivered by the first prototype.

# Summarize portfolio progress

Summarize completion across projects without replacing the task-level view. Origin: STORY.md, simulated opening user.

# Share an authenticated workspace

Eventually share plans across accounts with controlled access and centralized persistence. Origin: STORY.md, simulated opening user; no service is delivered in the prototype.

# See portfolio finish dates

Show predicted finish dates per project and for the whole portfolio. Origin: STORY.md, simulated opening user.

# Try a weekday finish-to-start prototype

Use UTC whole-day arithmetic and a topological traversal. Each successor starts on the next weekday after every predecessor finishes; duration includes its first workday. Weekends are excluded, holidays are not modeled. This tests calendar semantics before choosing a production scheduler. Origin: STORY.md, AI opening conclusion.

# Consider a hosted relational service

A future authenticated HTTP service with relational storage could support shared projects. It introduces operating/privacy costs and is intentionally NOT implemented in the first local prototype. A browser-only prototype must not be described as shared storage. Origin: STORY.md, AI opening conclusion.

# Try simple project rollups

Group tasks by project, show the latest task finish, and use unweighted mean completion as a prototype metric. This does not measure effort or establish confidence. Origin: STORY.md, AI opening conclusion.

# Consider greedy owner leveling

A later greedy resource pass might delay tasks for each owner after dependency scheduling. Ordering would affect results, so do not call it optimal. This is an unimplemented alternative, separate from basic scheduling. Origin: STORY.md, AI opening conclusion.

# Implement the local portfolio forecast experiment

model.js computes validated UTC weekday finish-to-start dates and simple project rollups. Six Node tests passed for the demo, weekend boundaries, order independence, bad dates/durations/IDs/progress, cycles/missing links, and rollup semantics. Named owners are only displayed: there is NO resource leveling or shared service. This prototype is not production scheduling. Browser presentation has not yet been exercised by an automated real-browser check.

# Show the read-only portfolio in a local browser

index.html, app.js and styles.css render a local read-only portfolio timeline and date table using native text and locally loaded scripts. No accounts, persistence, external requests, editing, or capacity optimization is implemented. JS syntax and six model tests passed; full browser interaction is not claimed. Open index.html directly, or serve this folder locally.

# Plan one personal renovation

Replace the business portfolio with one personal renovation plan. No projects, owners, accounts, progress rollups, or resource leveling. Origin: STORY.md, simulated redirect one.

# Keep every task date explicitly chosen

Let the person enter each task start/end date. Editing a task must not reschedule another. Origin: STORY.md, simulated redirect one.

# Include weekends

Personal work can occur on weekends. Draw every calendar day and count inclusive date ranges. Origin: STORY.md, simulated redirect one.

# Identify personal priorities

Give tasks low/normal/high priority labels, not percentage-complete metrics. Origin: STORY.md, simulated redirect one.

# Keep a portable local plan

Import/export a documented JSON format with validation before replacement. Warn about any future conversion; never call lossy conversion exact preservation. Origin: STORY.md, simulated redirect one.

# Keep work in this browser

Save valid edits locally when storage is available; explain session-only operation and storage failures. Do not contact a cloud service. Origin: STORY.md, simulated redirect one.

# Keep tasks independent

Remove dependencies and automatic date propagation from this personal experiment. Origin: STORY.md, simulated redirect one.

# Use inclusive manual calendar ranges

Represent start/end as validated ISO calendar dates. A same-day task occupies one day; weekends are ordinary days. This intentionally replaces the portfolio duration/dependency algorithm. Origin: STORY.md, AI redirect-one conclusion.

# Use localStorage with an explicit failure boundary

Use browser localStorage for convenient valid-plan autosave. If unavailable, keep the app usable in memory and warn. Corrupt saved bytes are not silently overwritten; explicit reset is needed to replace them. This is browser-local, not synchronization or guaranteed durable backup. Origin: STORY.md, AI redirect-one conclusion.

# Use a small version-one file format

A version:1 envelope holds title and tasks with id/title/start/end/priority. Reject invalid dates/ranges, duplicate IDs, and unknown versions before applying an import. This version describes the personal manual-date model, not all possible planning apps. Origin: STORY.md, AI redirect-one conclusion.

# Implement a local editable personal timeline

Native forms create/edit/delete tasks; a calendar Gantt/date table shows weekends and priorities. Local storage autosaves validated plans, warns on failure, and protects unreadable saved bytes until explicit reset. JSON export downloads a file; explicit confirmed import validates before replacement. Project strings use textContent. Seven model tests and syntax checks passed; this stage has no real-browser interaction check and is an educational prototype, not a tested backup/synchronization service.

# Plan one makerspace workshop

Replace the personal renovation experiment with one workshop plan. Do not restore portfolio grouping, named-owner optimization, priorities, accounts, or cloud storage. Origin: STORY.md, simulated redirect two.

# Forecast from work duration

Choose duration in positive Monday-Friday workdays rather than editing an end date. Recalculate a forecast, without claiming resource optimization. Origin: STORY.md, simulated redirect two.

# Explain prerequisite timing

Allow finish-to-start prerequisites. A task may start only after every prerequisite finishes, with no dependency cycles or missing references. Origin: STORY.md, simulated redirect two.

# Respect an earliest allowed start

A project start and optional task earliest date bound the forecast. Weekend bounds advance to Monday. Do not confuse an earliest date with a guaranteed appointment. Origin: STORY.md, simulated redirect two.

# Use a clear workshop calendar

Work Monday-Friday and exclude weekends. Explain that holidays, part days, and resource availability are not modeled. Origin: STORY.md, simulated redirect two.

# Explore a what-if without losing the baseline

Explicitly capture an immutable baseline, then change the current plan and compare dates visually/textually. Do not replace the baseline on each edit. Clearing/replacing it requires an explicit action. Origin: STORY.md, simulated redirect two.

# Edit the complete task set

Add, edit, select, and remove tasks using accessible forms. Reject deletion of a referenced prerequisite instead of silently detaching links. Failed edits keep the draft and valid plan. Origin: STORY.md, simulated redirect two.

# Explain conversion of personal plans

Keep JSON portability/local persistence, but preview conversion of version-one manual-date plans before replacing the current workshop. Make date/priority losses and changed weekday semantics explicit. Origin: STORY.md, simulated redirect two.

# Use iterative weekday finish-to-start forecasting

Use whole UTC days and deterministic topological traversal of all prerequisites. Start is the latest of normalized project start, normalized optional earliest date, and next workday after every predecessor finish. End is duration-1 workdays later. Reject cycles, missing/repeated/self links, invalid dates, excess tasks/durations, or a combined current/baseline chart horizon over 730 calendar days before applying a change. Maximum 100 tasks, duration 1-60 workdays, dates 2000-2100. These bounds keep a small DOM chart practical, not an optimal scheduler. No holidays or resource leveling. This is a NEW conclusion, not restoration/approval of the withdrawn portfolio scheduler. Origin: STORY.md, AI redirect-two conclusion.

# Use an explicit full-plan baseline snapshot

Capture a deep snapshot of validated plan data on explicit request; edits never mutate it. Render current and baseline forecasts on a common calendar axis, with text dates and finish deltas explicitly counted in calendar days. Removed baseline-only tasks remain visible. Added tasks have no baseline. This is a what-if comparison, not an approval state. Origin: STORY.md, AI redirect-two conclusion.

# Version the workshop file and preview legacy conversion

Use version:2 with title/start/tasks (id/title/duration/earliest/dependsOn) and an optional full baseline. Validate both forecasts and their common horizon. Import preview is session-only until Apply. Convert v1 manual ranges to at least one weekday of duration, preserve start as an earliest bound, drop priority, and add no dependencies. Explain that end dates/weekends/priorities no longer have the same meaning; do not silently convert stored v1 data or overwrite corrupt storage. Origin: STORY.md, AI redirect-two conclusion.

# Use a native local DOM chart and forms

Use dependency-free classic browser scripts, textContent, native controls, and a horizontally scrolling calendar grid. The application can load from local files or a local static server without a runtime API/CDN. File-origin localStorage support varies; show failures and recommend a stable local origin for persistence. Keep a text task table and distinct baseline/current bars. App task links are not SpecSpec justification links. Origin: STORY.md, AI redirect-two conclusion.

# Implement a native local Gantt editor with real browser evidence

Classic local scripts and native forms render current/baseline bars, a textual date table, weekend shading, editable prerequisites, and explicit baseline capture/replacement/clear. Valid edits autosave; corrupt/legacy saved bytes stay protected until explicit Apply/reset and can be downloaded unchanged. File and pasted JSON preview does not mutate the plan; stale file reads are cancelled. Dirty failed task drafts survive invalid cycles and cancelled navigation; resizing retains native caret/form identity and confines horizontal scroll to chart/table. Imported names use textContent. Twenty model tests, syntax checks, and a real installed Windows Chromium smoke test passed; desktop/narrow screenshots were inspected. Real browser checks exercised forecast changes, immutable baseline, cyclic drafts, safe deletion, literal markup text, actual download/file upload, preview/cancel/lossy v1 conversion, reload, protected/corrupt/legacy storage, storage denial, and direct file-origin launch. No external app requests occurred (native data-URL date icons are not network requests). This is dispatched browser evidence, not exhaustive manual/accessibility/platform/performance or production certification.
